main_way_in: type of object (what you travel in or on: car, motorcycle, bicycle, boat, caravan, aircraft); maker and model at the product step

Buyers' guides start from intended use inside the type (SlashGear motorcycles; AAA), and only the maker's own site leads with its ranges (Raleigh).

level1_groups: Cars; Vans, trucks and buses; Motorcycles, scooters and powered light rides; Bicycles and other cycles; Off-road, snow and utility vehicles; Caravans, motorhomes and trailers; Boats and watercraft; Aircraft; Rail and horse-drawn vehicles; Prams and strollers; Parts and accessories

This is a display regrouping of memo leaves, with no id change: the ten G1.1 leaves come up to level 1, so the memo's Land/Rail/Water/Air sub-family is not shown first. Cars = G1.1.1 by UNECE body order. Vans, trucks and buses = G1.1.2. Motorcycles = G1.1.3 by type (standard, cruiser, sport, touring, adventure, scooter, e-scooter). Bicycles = G1.1.5 by discipline (road, gravel, mountain, BMX, city, folding, cargo) plus G1.1.6. Off-road = G1.1.4. Caravans, motorhomes and trailers = G1.1.8 (towed, then driven) plus G1.1.7. Electric bikes get a shortcut view under Bicycles (attribute assist), not a group of their own.
quality_markers: Cars: reliability (few problems in daily use: problems per 100 vehicles at 90 days, then at 3 years) > safety (Euro NCAP stars, 0 to 5) > proven, mature technology over new and untried > build quality > size class against need (Autohome micro to large; separate ladders for SUV and MPV) > running costs. Bicycles: fit (frame size XS to XL) > intended riding (geometry for the discipline) > component level (groupset ladder, not yet attested) > frame material and weight. Motorcycles: intended riding > fit, checked on a test ride > running and ownership costs; looks and spec come last. Boats, caravans and aircraft: length or size and layout > condition and age (memo only; provisional)

main_way_in: type of property (home, mobile or floating home, land, outbuilding, commercial building, burial place); location is the main filter, never a level
reason: Portals and their apps divide by property type, and Japan's also divides by new or pre-owned (SUUMO categories; immowelt property type after rent or buy). Rightmove asks for location first, but the owner rule says countries and places never divide a category, so location is the main filter and type is the way in. Every buying guide checks condition, legal title and fit after location (Barfoot and Thompson; ANZ; e.surv).
ladder: What kind of property? > Which type (house by attachment, flat or maisonette, park or floating home, land by use, building by function)? > What makes a good one, filtered by location, price, bedrooms, tenure, new or pre-owned and energy band?
level1_groups: Houses and flats; Park, mobile and floating homes; Land and farms; Garden buildings and outbuildings; Commercial buildings; Burial places
level2_note: Not built as kinds (nodes only, so no groups file). The groups map to existing nodes. Houses and flats = G2.2.1 (detached, semi-detached, terraced), G2.2.2 (flat, maisonette) and G2.2.3. Park, mobile and floating homes = G2.2.4, ordered least to most fixed. Land and farms = G2.1.1 to G2.1.7 by use: building plot first, then farm land, woodland, water, mixed holding. Garden buildings and outbuildings = G2.3.1 to G2.3.6 by what the building is for (shelter, storage, garden rooms, animal buildings, shade and surfaces, pools). Commercial buildings = G2.3.7. Burial places = G2.4. Buying and renting: only buying is a possession, so the portals' first 'buy or rent' choice is not shown (rent is out of scope).
quality_markers: Homes: location and neighbourhood (filter and map, weighed first by every guide) > structural condition (roof, walls, damp and plumbing, wiring and heating) > legal title and tenure (freehold > share of freehold > leasehold; title and LIM checks) > energy performance and orientation (EPC A to G) > fit to the household (bedrooms, layout, garden, parking). Land: principal use and land quality (ALC grade 1 > 2 > 3a > 3b > 4 > 5, memo) > access and water > area. Factory-built homes and garden buildings: build standard (residential BS 3632 against holiday BS EN 1647, HUD code; memo) > maker's range and materials (provisional). Burial places: memo only (in-ground or above, capacity); provisional

Proposed scoped revision: owner for factory-built kinds (G2.2.4 park homes, lodges, static caravans, park models, tiny houses on wheels and floating homes; the kit-built G2.3 garden buildings; pool shells in G2.3.6). There the maker enters as the owner of a range or model (memo section 6). Provisional.

structure_flags: SUUMO splits new from pre-owned at the top. Keep that as a build_history facet with a shortcut (C5), not a level. Rental is shown first by every portal but is out of scope as a possession; confirm in the next decision pass. Location, station and commute time are filters for listings, but G2 stores no listing (C16). So the G2 pages act as buying guides over kinds and named forms, and the location facets apply only where a page links to outside listings. Decide this in the decision pass. The EPC and RICS schemes need registry rows (C4c, C16 grading-scale registry). Burial places and commercial buildings have no evidence in HOL_EV_9; keep the memo calls, provisional. The evidence is Anglosphere- and Japan-heavy; no continental European or Asian portal page loaded beyond app-store pages.

level2_note: Not built (no kinds in data). The groups map one to one onto memo sub-families A to H, kept in the memo's ordered placement test. Level 2 is the memo leaves where they exist: A by contact area (external, internal, dual); D by how it meets the body (enclosing, ring or sleeve, pump); E by action (restraints, deprivation and gags, impact and sensation, chastity, electro-stimulation). USP Class VI and ISO 10993 biocompatibility and the EU phthalate limit of 0.1 percent (class i attributes, memo). Lovehoney Awards (Customer Favorite, Staff Favorite, Couples' Choice, Best Innovation; judging not stated): a retailer label, so dated platform_tag (class vi), not a tier. my-best in-house rankings (no published method): class iii editorial tier entries with low weight.
